title: Sparse labels across script changes

known_project_facts.project: An academic fellowship office links applicant histories across two annual intake systems; identity is the individual applicant, not family or institution.
known_project_facts.data: Names use Arabic, Latin and Devanagari scripts, sometimes switched between years. Latin transliterations are inconsistent. Many applicants omit date of birth; family contact phones and institutional email addresses are shared.
known_project_facts.labels: 80 adjudicated links, mostly Latin-script applicants, and 100 easy non-links from dissimilar names. No representative multilingual held-out set.
known_project_facts.current_pipeline: ASCII-folded name prefix blocks and edit distance on flattened names. A team proposes a multilingual embedding encoder and supervised neural matcher.
known_project_facts.constraints: Offline processing; CPU-only service; one researcher has two days per month for adjudication. Keep original strings and source provenance. False merges can combine confidential applicant histories.

explicitly_unknown: Which language/script and source slices exist and need evaluation?
How are name order, shared contacts and missing attributes encoded?
What validated labels or runtime evidence justify a learned alternative?
